HOA BOARD ELECTION PROCEDURES — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association · September 2, 2026

HOA BOARD ELECTION PROCEDURES — INTRODUCTION AND SCOPE
This information sheet describes, in general terms, the secret-ballot election procedures that apply to a California common interest development association under the Davis-Stirling Common Interest Development Act, Civil Code §§ 5100–5145, in connection with Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association. It covers when those procedures apply, the requirement that the association adopt its own election operating rules, the requirement that an independent third party conduct the election, and the statutory notice-timing and double-envelope ballot mechanics. This topic is distinct from a seller's document-disclosure obligations to a buyer under the Davis-Stirling Act's disclosure article (addressed in this corpus's HOA/CC&R Disclosure document), from an association's lien and foreclosure remedy for unpaid assessments (addressed in this corpus's HOA Assessment Lien and Foreclosure — Information Sheet), and from the recording mechanics that create a common interest development in the first place (addressed in this corpus's Common Interest Development Formation — Information Sheet). This sheet is informational only. It does not itself call, notice, conduct, or certify any election; it does not select, appoint, or evaluate any inspector of elections; it does not adopt, amend, or interpret any specific association's election operating rules or governing documents; and it does not determine whether any actual election, notice, ballot procedure, or vote count relating to Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association has complied — or failed to comply — with the statutory requirements it describes.

WHEN THE SECRET-BALLOT ELECTION PROCEDURES APPLY
California law does not require every association vote to be conducted by secret ballot — it specifies particular categories of votes to which the secret-ballot procedures apply. Civil Code § 5100(a)(1) provides: "Notwithstanding any other law or provision of the governing documents, elections regarding assessments legally requiring a vote, election and removal of directors, amendments to the governing documents, or the grant of exclusive use of common area pursuant to Section 4600 shall be held by secret ballot in accordance with the procedures set forth in this article." Section 5100(a)(2) adds a timing requirement specific to director elections: "An association shall hold an election for a seat on the board of directors in accordance with the procedures set forth in this article at the expiration of the corresponding director's term and at least once every four years." Section 5100(b) extends the article to "any topic that is expressly identified in the operating rules as being governed by this article," and Section 5100(c) makes the article apply "to both incorporated and unincorporated associations, notwithstanding any contrary provision of the governing documents." Section 5100(d) limits the article to "votes cast directly by the membership," not votes cast by delegates or other elected representatives, and Section 5100(e) provides that this article prevails over any conflicting election provision of the Nonprofit Mutual Benefit Corporation Law. Section 5100(f) provides an exception where a director seat is not filled by election: directors "shall not be required to be elected pursuant to this article if the governing documents provide that one member from each separate interest is a director." This scope provision concerns Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association in general terms; it does not determine whether any specific vote by Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association's membership falls within one of these categories.

  — Cal. Civ. Code § 5100(a)(1) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 5100(a)(1) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=5100.)

  — Cal. Civ. Code § 5100(a)(2) (California Legislative Information text), Civ. C. § 5100(a)(2) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=5100.)
  Known gap: All quoted material in this clause comes from subsections (a) through (f) of a single statutory section, Civil Code § 5100; it is one source, not independent corroborating sources, even though it is presented as several numbered points. As verified against the current statutory text, § 5100(a)(1) itself requires secret-ballot procedures for "election and removal of directors" without qualifying that requirement by whether the election is contested or by how many candidates are nominated — a narrower assumption (that the secret-ballot requirement is limited to contested director elections, or triggers only once nominations exceed open seats) is not supported by the text of § 5100 as fetched. California law does contain a related but separate and narrower mechanism, at Civil Code § 5103, allowing (not requiring) an association to seat qualified candidates "by acclamation" without a secret ballot when nominations do not exceed the number of open seats and several additional conditions are met; that section was fetched only once during this research (not independently double-verified under this document's verification protocol) and its contents are accordingly not described or quoted here, so as not to state anything about it that has not been confirmed. This is one state's statute, used as evidence of California's HOA board-election framework — not a claim about which state's law governs a specific association; other states impose different or no comparable secret-ballot requirements.

ADOPTION OF ELECTION OPERATING RULES
California law requires an association to adopt its own written election operating rules, through a specified rulemaking procedure, and requires those rules to address a defined list of subjects. Civil Code § 5105(a) provides: "An association shall adopt operating rules in accordance with the procedures prescribed by Article 5 (commencing with Section 4340) of Chapter 3, that do all of the following:" Among the items that follow, § 5105(a)(3) requires the rules to "[s]pecify the qualifications for candidates for the board and any other elected position, subject to subdivision (b), and procedures for the nomination of candidates, consistent with the governing documents," adding that "[a] nomination or election procedure shall not be deemed reasonable if it disallows any member from nominating themself for election to the board." Section 5105(a)(5) requires the rules to "[s]pecify a method of selecting one or three independent third parties as inspector or inspectors of elections," by board appointment, member election, "[or] any other method for selecting the inspector or inspectors." The rules must also, among other things, ensure equal access to association media and to common-area meeting space for candidates and members campaigning on either side of an issue (§ 5105(a)(1)-(2)); specify voting power, proxy rules, and the voting period (§ 5105(a)(4)); and require retention of a candidate registration list and a voter list as association election materials, with a process for members to verify and correct their own listed information (§ 5105(a)(6)-(7)). Section 5105(h)(4) further requires the rules to obligate the inspector of elections to "deliver, or cause to be delivered, at least 30 days before an election, to each member both of the following documents: (A) The ballot or ballots. (B) A copy of the election operating rules," and provides that rules adopted under this section "shall not be amended less than 90 days prior to an election." These requirements concern any election operating rules Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association adopts; this clause does not itself adopt, amend, or interpret any specific association's rules.

The full list of required subjects in § 5105(a) runs to seven enumerated paragraphs, and § 5105 as a whole runs considerably longer than reproduced here, including a separate framework in subdivisions (b) through (g) governing when and how an association may disqualify a nominee (for example, for not being current on regular or special assessments, subject to statutory exceptions) and a separate optional framework in subdivision (i) for electronic secret ballots; a generic assumption that the statute's list is limited to "candidate qualifications, campaigning, ballot procedures" understates its breadth (it also covers proxies, quorum-related voting-period rules, the method of selecting the inspector of elections, and record retention) without being wrong about those three examples themselves. This clause also does not quote or verify the separate rulemaking procedure incorporated by reference, Article 5 (commencing with Section 4340) of Chapter 3, or the disqualification framework in § 5105(b)-(g); those were not independently fetched and verified for this document. This is one state's statute, used as evidence of California's HOA board-election framework — not a claim about which state's law governs a specific association; other states impose different or no comparable requirement that an association adopt election operating rules.

THE INDEPENDENT THIRD PARTY WHO CONDUCTS THE ELECTION
California law requires that an association's election be conducted by an independent third party, and defines both who qualifies and who is disqualified from serving in that role. Civil Code § 5110(a) provides: "The association shall select an independent third party or parties as an inspector of elections. The number of inspectors of elections shall be one or three." Section 5110(b) explains who may — and may not — serve: "an independent third party includes, but is not limited to, a volunteer poll worker with the county registrar of voters, a licensee of the California Board of Accountancy, or a notary public. An independent third party may be a member, but may not be a director or a candidate for director or be related to a director or to a candidate for director. An independent third party may not be a person, business entity, or subdivision of a business entity who is currently employed or under contract to the association for any compensable services other than serving as an inspector of elections." Section 5110(c) lists the inspector's duties, including determining the number of memberships entitled to vote, determining the validity of proxies, receiving ballots, hearing and determining challenges to the right to vote, counting and tabulating votes, determining when polls close, and determining the tabulated results. Section 5110(d) requires the inspector or inspectors to "perform all duties impartially, in good faith, to the best of the inspector or inspectors of elections' ability, as expeditiously as is practical, and in a manner that protects the interest of all members of the association," and provides that where there are three inspectors, "the decision or act of a majority shall be effective in all respects as the decision or act of all." This description concerns the inspector-of-elections requirement generally; it does not identify, evaluate, or disqualify any specific person as an inspector of elections for Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association.

NOTICE TIMING AND THE DOUBLE-ENVELOPE SECRET-BALLOT PROCEDURE
California law sets specific notice-timing requirements for a director election and a specific double-envelope mechanism for preserving ballot secrecy. Civil Code § 5115(a) provides, for elections of directors and recall elections: "An association shall provide general notice of the procedure and deadline for submitting a nomination at least 30 days before any deadline for submitting a nomination." Section 5115(b) separately requires the association to give general notice of the ballot-return date, time, and address, of the meeting at which a quorum will be determined and ballots counted, and of the list of candidates' names, "at least 30 days before the ballots are distributed." Section 5115(c) then requires that "[b]allots and two preaddressed envelopes with instructions on how to return ballots shall be mailed by first-class mail or delivered by the association to every member not less than 30 days prior to the deadline for voting," and describes the resulting double-envelope mechanism: "The ballot itself is not signed by the voter, but is inserted into an envelope that is sealed. This envelope is inserted into a second envelope that is sealed. In the upper left-hand corner of the second envelope, the voter shall sign the voter's name, indicate the voter's name, and indicate the address or separate interest identifier that entitles the voter to vote." That second, signed envelope is then addressed to the inspector or inspectors of elections for tabulation. Section 5115(d) addresses a separate topic, quorum: if the governing documents require a quorum for a director election and it is not met, the association may adjourn to a reconvened meeting at least 20 days later, at which a 20 percent quorum (voting in person, by proxy, or by secret ballot) applies unless the governing documents set a lower figure. These notice-timing and ballot-secrecy requirements apply generally to a director election conducted by Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association; this clause does not itself calculate any specific deadline or verify that any particular notice or mailing by Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association met these requirements.

The recurring '30 days' figure across subsections (a), (b), and (c) is the same statutory period restated for three distinct notice-and-mailing steps (nomination-deadline notice, pre-distribution ballot-logistics notice, and the ballot-and-envelope mailing itself), not three independently-confirmed different figures; a generic assumption of a single undifferentiated notice period would obscure that these are three separate 30-day deadlines tied to three different triggering events, and the reconvened-meeting quorum period in subdivision (d) is a distinct 20-day figure for a different purpose. HOW BALLOTS ARE COUNTED, TABULATED, AND REPORTED
California law requires that ballots be counted in public, restricts who may handle ballots before the count, and sets a deadline for reporting results. Civil Code § 5120(a) provides: "All votes shall be counted and tabulated by the inspector or inspectors of elections, or the designee of the inspector or inspectors of elections, in public at a properly noticed open meeting of the board or members. Any candidate or other member of the association may witness the counting and tabulation of the votes. A person, including a member of the association or an employee of the management company, shall not open or otherwise review any ballot before the time and place at which the ballots are counted and tabulated." The same subdivision allows the inspector to "verify the member's information and signature on the outer envelope prior to the meeting at which ballots are tabulated," and provides that "[o]nce a secret ballot is received by the inspector or inspectors of elections, it shall be irrevocable." Section 5120(b) then sets a reporting deadline: "The tabulated results of the election shall be promptly reported to the board and shall be recorded in the minutes of the next meeting of the board and shall be available for review by members of the association. Within 15 days of the election, the board shall give general notice pursuant to Section 4045 of the tabulated results of the election." Section 5120(c) extends the same before-the-count restriction to electronic ballots: a person "shall not open or otherwise review any tally sheet of votes cast by electronic secret ballots before the time and place at which the ballots are counted and tabulated." These counting, reporting, and confidentiality requirements apply generally to an election conducted by Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association; this clause does not itself count, tabulate, or report the results of any specific election.

expectedJSON.body: California law sets specific notice-timing requirements for a director election and a specific double-envelope mechanism for preserving ballot secrecy. Civil Code § 5115(a) provides, for elections of directors and recall elections: "An association shall provide general notice of the procedure and deadline for submitting a nomination at least 30 days before any deadline for submitting a nomination." Section 5115(b) separately requires the association to give general notice of the ballot-return date, time, and address, of the meeting at which a quorum will be determined and ballots counted, and of the list of candidates' names, "at least 30 days before the ballots are distributed." Section 5115(c) then requires that "[b]allots and two preaddressed envelopes with instructions on how to return ballots shall be mailed by first-class mail or delivered by the association to every member not less than 30 days prior to the deadline for voting," and describes the resulting double-envelope mechanism: "The ballot itself is not signed by the voter, but is inserted into an envelope that is sealed. This envelope is inserted into a second envelope that is sealed. In the upper left-hand corner of the second envelope, the voter shall sign the voter's name, indicate the voter's name, and indicate the address or separate interest identifier that entitles the voter to vote." That second, signed envelope is then addressed to the inspector or inspectors of elections for tabulation. Section 5115(d) addresses a separate topic, quorum: if the governing documents require a quorum for a director election and it is not met, the association may adjourn to a reconvened meeting at least 20 days later, at which a 20 percent quorum (voting in person, by proxy, or by secret ballot) applies unless the governing documents set a lower figure. These notice-timing and ballot-secrecy requirements apply generally to a director election conducted by Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association; this clause does not itself calculate any specific deadline or verify that any particular notice or mailing by Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association met these requirements.

expectedJSON.body: California law requires that ballots be counted in public, restricts who may handle ballots before the count, and sets a deadline for reporting results. Civil Code § 5120(a) provides: "All votes shall be counted and tabulated by the inspector or inspectors of elections, or the designee of the inspector or inspectors of elections, in public at a properly noticed open meeting of the board or members. Any candidate or other member of the association may witness the counting and tabulation of the votes. A person, including a member of the association or an employee of the management company, shall not open or otherwise review any ballot before the time and place at which the ballots are counted and tabulated." The same subdivision allows the inspector to "verify the member's information and signature on the outer envelope prior to the meeting at which ballots are tabulated," and provides that "[o]nce a secret ballot is received by the inspector or inspectors of elections, it shall be irrevocable." Section 5120(b) then sets a reporting deadline: "The tabulated results of the election shall be promptly reported to the board and shall be recorded in the minutes of the next meeting of the board and shall be available for review by members of the association. Within 15 days of the election, the board shall give general notice pursuant to Section 4045 of the tabulated results of the election." Section 5120(c) extends the same before-the-count restriction to electronic ballots: a person "shall not open or otherwise review any tally sheet of votes cast by electronic secret ballots before the time and place at which the ballots are counted and tabulated." These counting, reporting, and confidentiality requirements apply generally to an election conducted by Sunnyvale Meadows Homeowners Association; this clause does not itself count, tabulate, or report the results of any specific election.
